//: The bench, explained to agents. One entry per logging capability, queryable through the stream_guide tool and served as MCP prompts. House rule: every logging capability ships with a detailed README entry AND a detailed entry here - an agent should never have to guess what a topic means.

power.what: CPU package watts, thermal pressure, fan RPM, CPU/GPU die temperatures, aggregate CPU as one scalar, and the top energy consumers attached to every sample. macOS, sampled every 10s by default.
power.read: Readings are DEBUG metric events (power.package_w, power.cpu_pct, power.cpu_die_c, power.gpu_die_c, power.fan_rpm, power.speed_limit_pct). Threshold crossings are edge-triggered WARN/ERROR and announce recovery. The 'top by energy' events name the processes responsible, with pid and %cpu.
power.gotchas: power_unavailable: not root in fields means powermetrics has no privilege - thermals and CPU still flow, watts do not; run scripts/install-power-tailer.sh once. A speed_limit_pct under 100 is the machine itself throttling: that IS the too-much-power signal, no tuning needed. Aggregate cpu_pct is a sum over cores (1258 means ~12.6 cores busy).

dl.what: A download in flight: percent, bytes and rate as metric events (dl.pct, dl.mb, dl.rate_mbs), one verdict when it ends. Wraps curl/wget/hf transparently or watches the destination path directly (--watch), which is the honest aggregate for multi-shard Hugging Face pulls.
dl.read: A stall is edge-triggered: one WARN after --stall seconds of no movement, one ERROR at three times that ('treating as dead'), one INFO on recovery. 'done:' INFO is success; 'failed: (exit N)' ERROR carries the wrapped command's exit status.
dl.gotchas: Watch-mode percent can DROP after a relaunch when the producer restarts its output file by design - a drop then racing is a re-stream, not data loss. Short 0.0MB/s windows are normal (retry backoff, shard gaps); trust the stall events, not a single zero sample.

build.what: A build or test run wrapped: one event per compiler diagnostic with src file:line, one verdict with exit status, duration and counts. Knows clang/gcc (and their drivers' own 'clang: error:'), cmake, make, rustc, npm, xcodebuild, Vivado/Quartus, and LINKERS: Apple ld/lld, GNU 'undefined reference'/'multiple definition' (which carry no severity word), duplicate symbols, collect2.
build.read: lake/ninja/make progress lines are DEBUG readings carrying a build.progress_pct metric - an hours-long Lean or mathlib build charts like a download. Filter level>=WARN for diagnostics. The verdict fields carry errors/warnings counts; 'exited 0 DESPITE N errors' means the build lied about success. Sanitizer (ASan/TSan/UBSan) and valgrind findings arrive WHOLE as single events with the full report in fields.report.
build.gotchas: Every event of one build shares a trace - query by trace to see one build end to end. Compiler snippet/caret lines are folded into fields.snippet, not separate events.

fs.what: A directory tree as it changes: created/modified INFO, deleted WARN, bursts collapsed into one summary. With --diff, the changed LINES: one event per hunk with removed (-) and added (+) lines together in the message.
fs.read: Hunks of one save share a trace with their 'modified' anchor - query by trace for the whole edit. fields.change is created|modified|deleted|diff|burst.
fs.gotchas: Idempotent by content hash: a rewrite with identical bytes publishes NOTHING, so silence after a save can mean no real change. fields.undiffable = binary|big|budget explains a modified event with no hunks.

sys.what: The machine's own life events, macOS: crash reports and kernel panics parsed from DiagnosticReports (process, exception, signal), resource diagnostics, the previous shutdown cause once per boot, volume mount/unmount/RENAME, and sleep/wake.
sys.read: A crash is ERROR, a panic CRITICAL, a resource diagnostic WARN. 'previous shutdown' at ERROR means the machine did not shut down cleanly - the cause code is translated in the message. A volume 'renamed' WARN means every path on that volume just moved: correlate it against writes that died at the same moment. Wake events explain gaps in every other stream.
sys.gotchas: Reports newer than --backfill (default 1h) are published at startup because a crash lands its report BEFORE the reboot; do not treat a startup burst as fresh crashes - check fields.at for when each actually happened. 'unreadable' WARN means system reports exist that this user cannot open (needs _analyticsusers membership).

vitals.what: Disk, memory, CPU load per host, local or over ssh. Readings are DEBUG metric events (disk.used_pct, mem.used_pct, load.per_core); threshold crossings are edge-triggered WARN/ERROR with recovery announced.
vitals.read: load.per_core over 1 is busy, over 2 is drowning. Read-only filesystems are deliberately excluded from disk alerts.
vitals.gotchas: A threshold event appears ONCE per crossing - absence of WARN does not mean recent, check the DEBUG readings' timestamps.

gpu.what: GPU utilisation, memory, temperature, power via whichever vendor tool exists (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi, ioreg, vcgencmd). Metrics gpu.utilization_pct, gpu.memory_used_mb, gpu.temperature_c, gpu.power_w.
gpu.read: Edge-triggered temperature/memory crossings; Raspberry Pi under-voltage and throttle flags are ERROR/WARN.
gpu.gotchas: A missing reading is absent, never zero - macOS cards without sensors report no temperature at all.

apps-sdk.topics: cpp.<app>, c.<app>, rust.<app>, python.<app>, go.<app>, java.<app>, swift.<app>, fortran.<app>, ocaml.<app>, lean.<app>, haskell.<app>, ruby.<app>, scala.<app>, shell.<app>, node.<app>, web.<app>
apps-sdk.what: Programs instrumented with the SDKs, one topic per app per language. Kotlin and Scala ride the Java SDK; Rails rides Ruby's ::Logger adapter; six SDKs hook the language's own logging framework so existing log lines arrive with no call sites changed.
apps-sdk.read: Levels are the producer's own. Uncaught exceptions arrive with stacks even when nobody logged them. Events may carry a trace - the same id crosses HTTP to other tiers, so /recent?trace= stitches one action across languages.
apps-sdk.gotchas: Every SDK is DEVELOPMENT xor PRODUCTION with no default, and production ships NOTHING by default - an app that publishes nothing may simply be built in production mode, which is the design, not a bug.

os-app.what: OS logs (macOS unified log, journald, Windows event log) and known app/service logs (postgres, nginx, redis, kafka...; Unity's Editor.log and Unreal's per-project editor logs, level-parsed by their own conventions). Local, docker, or pulled over ssh.
os-app.read: Levels come from the source's own format where one exists (postgres LOG->INFO, Unreal 'Warning:'->WARN, Unity 'error CS...'->ERROR).
os-app.gotchas: os.<host> is scoped (kernel by default on macOS) - an app you expect may need its own tailer, see 'superlog-tail apps'.

dl-power-bridge-note.what: superlog-bridge relays a remote hub's WHOLE feed here verbatim over an ssh tunnel - same topics, same events. A topic like build.<otherhost> or power.<otherhost> arriving on this bench may originate on another machine's hub.
dl-power-bridge-note.read: Indistinguishable from local streams by design; origin.device names the real machine.
dl-power-bridge-note.gotchas: One direction only - never bridge two hubs at each other (feedback loop).

gas.what: Operational key balances on chain - native gas coin or ERC-20 - polled per key from a gitignored config with per-key thresholds. Readings are DEBUG metric events (gas.<label>). Four wire dialects behind one discipline: EVM JSON-RPC (native + ERC-20), Solana JSON-RPC (native + SPL via getTokenAccountsByOwner, several token accounts summed), TronGrid REST (native + TRC-20 balanceOf; an account Tron has never seen reads as zero, honestly - unactivated pays for gas as badly as empty), and Esplora REST for Bitcoin (funded minus spent).
gas.read: CRITICAL means a key is below its fund-now line - a production keeper/oracle is about to stop; it is said ONCE per crossing. WARN is below the low line. 'recovered: ... funded' INFO closes the incident. 'rpc-down' WARN means the chain endpoint is unreachable, not that keys are empty.
gas.gotchas: Absence of CRITICAL does not mean healthy-right-now - check the DEBUG readings' timestamps and values. Balances are telemetry precision, not accounting. Token keys read balanceOf with the config's decimals; a wrong decimals value is off by orders of magnitude.

net.what: HTTP/S calls through the logging proxy (one event per request/response with status and latency), gRPC with status from trailers, listening-port changes, DNS records and TLS expiry watched for change. net.<host>.state is the network's own state watched for change: interface addresses, default gateway, Wi-Fi SSID, VPN tunnels, DNS resolver set, new LAN devices, plus --ping targets with RTT/loss readings. superlog-dns --asn also watches which AS originates each domain's prefix (via RIPEstat).
net.read: 5xx is ERROR, 4xx WARN. New PUBLIC listener is WARN; NS/CAA changes are WARN (that is how domains get taken); certs WARN at 3 weeks out. netstate: VPN down / DHCP renumber / resolver change are WARN (the 'everything just broke' class); gateway MAC change is ERROR (router swap or ARP spoof); a dead ping target is an ERROR edge whose traceroute diagnosis arrives on the SAME trace id - query /recent?trace= to read alarm and diagnosis together. dns --asn: origin AS change or prefix withdrawal is CRITICAL - what a hijack looks like from outside.
net.gotchas: dns and ports diff snapshots - the first poll is a silent baseline, only changes are events. netstate reports ARP first-sights once and never reports cache expiry (churn teaches muting); ping loss must persist two checks before the edge fires. RTT/loss are DEBUG metric readings every interval by design.

history.what: The live ring at /recent is only minutes deep. search_history reads the on-disk journal (superlog-journal/) for hours or days back, with the same filters incl. trace.
history.read: Prefer search_history for 'what happened at 3am'; tail_logs/search_logs for now.
history.gotchas: The journal only holds what reached the hub while the journal writer ran.

alarms.what: The alarm blotter's feed, sparse by construction. alert.<rule> comes from superlog-alert's rules over the bench's own streams (level / rate / silence / combo-of-conditions); alert.inbound.* comes from production systems POSTing superlog-alarm's public webhook through a tunnel - deduped by key, repeats counted, heartbeat dead-man included.
alarms.read: One firing = one event per occurrence with fields.key and fields.repeat; the same key at repeat 113 is ONE ongoing alarm, not 113. 'RECOVERED: <key> after <duration> (fired Nx)' at INFO closes it. monitor_dead:<name> at CRITICAL means a production CHECKER stopped heartbeating - every alarm it owns is blind until it recovers. P0=CRITICAL, P1=ERROR, P2=WARN.
alarms.gotchas: Rules never match alert.* (loop guard), so inbound alarms bypass the rules engine by design - they are already alarms. Absence of events means healthy OR the gateway is down: check gateway /healthz (firing keys, heartbeats, tunnel state, channel roster). The gateway's POST returns 502 when the hub write fails, so producers know an alarm did NOT land. Every event of one firing after the first says 'still firing' - dedup lives in the GATEWAY, so bypassing it (posting alert.inbound.* straight to the hub) forfeits repeat counts and recovery.

wh.*.what: Captured webhook deliveries - the bench's webhook TESTER. The alarm gateway provisions public capture endpoints (one click in either viewer, or many from a --provision endpoints.json manifest); anything POSTed to that URL - a Stripe event, a GitHub hook, a partner's callback - lands here as one event per delivery. A 'relay' endpoint additionally hands each delivery to a local handler and returns the handler's real response to the sender (stripe listen semantics, with a bench record).
wh.*.read: msg is '<METHOD> /hook/<name> (<bytes>b[, sig ok|BAD][, relay <status>])'; fields carry method, content-type, user-agent, stripe-signature / x-github-event when present, and the body up to 32KB (real Stripe events run 5-15KB and arrive whole). fields.sig appears ONLY when the endpoint has a signing secret ('secret' in the manifest, or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET): 'verified', 'FAILED' (WARN - tampered or wrong secret), or 'verified, but timestamp Ns old - replay?' (WARN). fields.relay_status is the local handler's HTTP status, or 'unreachable (...)' at WARN - the handler being down is the finding a relay endpoint exists to produce. Absent sig field means no secret was configured, not that verification failed.
wh.*.gotchas: Endpoints from the one-click button or the manifest ride ephemeral quick tunnels and DIE with the gateway - re-provision after a restart (the manifest does this automatically; URLs change). The current URL for every endpoint is in endpoints.env beside the gateway, rewritten on every change - read that file rather than guessing. Route health is in gateway /healthz under 'tunnels': healthy true/false/null with last_checked, last_ms and per-route ping intervals; null means not yet measured (a fresh tunnel name takes seconds to reach DNS), and two consecutive ping failures raise tunnel_down:<name> as an alarm. POST /selftest (loopback) round-trips EVERY route: capture endpoints must land a probe back on the hub, forwarded ports answering 502 report 'tunnel up, your service is not'.

sql.*.what: SQL on the bench, two engines. Postgres: superlog-sql holds LISTEN <channel> open, so any trigger, stored procedure or batch job publishes with one built-in statement - NOTIFY superlog, '{"level":"ERROR","msg":"..."}' - no extensions, no privileges beyond NOTIFY. SQLite: the database FILE is watched from outside the process (the header's own change counter, page count, -wal growth) - no lock taken, no library. Both engines can poll --query "name=SELECT ..." into DEBUG metrics on a slower clock.
sql.*.read: Postgres events carry the payload as msg; a JSON payload's level/msg/fields are honored, plain text arrives as INFO verbatim, fields.pid is the notifying backend. SQLite 'database changed' at INFO means transactions reached the main file (counter delta in the msg); 'writes in the WAL' means committed-but-not-checkpointed activity. sqlite.db_bytes / sqlite.wal_bytes are readings. A failing --query is ONE WARN until it recovers - silence about a query means it is answering.
sql.*.gotchas: NOTIFY delivery latency is bounded by the tailer's --interval heartbeat (psql only surfaces notifications when a command completes), default 1s. Notifications are NOT queued for absent listeners: events sent while the tailer is down are gone - the tailer says so with a WARN/RECOVERED pair around any gap. The SQLite change counter only bumps at checkpoint in WAL mode, which is why WAL growth is watched separately. In-process SQLite apps should use their language's SDK; this stream is the outside observer.

usb.*.what: The machine's USB device tree, watched by superlog-usb (ioreg on macOS, lsusb on Linux): hotplug events snapshot-diffed ('plugged in: iPhone (Apple Inc., serial ...)' at INFO, 'unplugged: ...' likewise), and the whole normalized tree as fields.tree (JSON: {name, vendor, serial, speed, children[]}) republished on every change.
usb.*.read: To answer 'is the phone connected', take the LATEST event with fields.tree for the host and walk it - the viewers' Devices window does exactly this, headlining handsets. Plug/unplug events give the timeline; the tree gives the current truth. A viewer refresh POSTs 127.0.0.1:7338/poll (loopback poke) to measure now instead of at the next 5s tick.
usb.*.gotchas: Handset recognition in the viewers is a name heuristic (iPhone/Android/Pixel/...); the tree below it is ground truth for anything the heuristic misses. macOS system_profiler's USB reporter returns nothing on some builds - the tailer reads the IORegistry instead, which always answers. fields.tree is capped at 16KB.

agents.what: Who is working the bench. Three kinds, one topic family: LISTENING - the MCP server announces every consumer from its initialize handshake, so agents appear the moment they connect; REQUESTING - each tool call as a DEBUG event with the tool and a summary of its arguments; REPORTING - the agent_report tool (or one POST to agent.<name>): which LLM the agent runs on, current status, the overall task, percent, and interval_s, the cadence it promises.
agents.read: One row per agent in the viewers' Agents window: name, llm, latest status, last seen. The freshness light is the agent's OWN promised cadence (default 900s = 15 min): green inside 2x, late inside 4x, silent beyond - an agent that broke its own word LOOKS like it. For an 8-hour job, report every 15 minutes AND on events (milestone, WARN/ERROR when the status IS the problem, done). Identity fields are sticky in the viewers - a requesting DEBUG does not erase who you are.
agents.gotchas: agent_report is the ONE deliberate write the otherwise read-only MCP server performs, and it can only land on agent.* topics - the read-only posture for logs is unchanged. The LLM is self-declared (the MCP handshake only names the client app, not the model), so llm is required in agent_report and absent means unreported, not unknown-and-guessed. Silence on the blotter is late/grey, not dead: pair a critical agent with an alarm-gateway heartbeat for a CRITICAL monitor_dead.

prs.what: Pull requests watched by superlog-prs (gh carries the wire, auth included): every open PR by the configured --author logins anywhere on GitHub, plus open PRs on --repo repos, plus the author's recently closed PRs. Whose move it is - waiting_on us or them - is computed from the record: the last non-bot word. Born from a 51-day silence that turned a changes-requested review into a stale-close.
prs.read: One DEBUG row per PR per poll: fields.waiting_on, days_waiting (also a metric for charting), changes_requested, last_actor, url. Crossings are edges: WARN when waiting-on-us passes --warn-days (default 3), ERROR at 3x, INFO recovery on reply; MERGED is INFO, CLOSED WITHOUT MERGE is ERROR. Crossings also fire the alarm gateway with dedup key pr:<repo>#<n> - one alarm with repeat counts, recovery closing the loop, notification channels included.
prs.gotchas: Waiting-on-us is the last-word rule: replying without addressing the review flips it to 'them' honestly - the clock measures conversation, not completion. The author search only sees the logins you configured; a PR authored by an unconfigured account is invisible (add every working account). gh must be authenticated; rate limits are generous at the default 300s poll but shorten intervals with care.

starlink.what: The Starlink dish, watched over its LAN gRPC API (192.168.100.1:9200, grpcurl with server reflection carries the wire). Readings each poll: starlink.pop_latency_ms, pop_drop_rate, down_mbps/up_mbps, obstruction_pct, gps_sats, uptime_s. Edges: each alert flag (thermal throttle, motors stuck, ...) is WARN when it appears and recovered when it clears; currently-obstructed likewise; dish unreachable is ERROR after two misses; firmware updates and reboots are one INFO each.
starlink.read: Chart the readings; trust the edges. pop_drop_rate is often ABSENT - the dish did not report it, which is not zero. Pair with net.<host>.state: dish unreachable + gateway unreachable = the router; dish unreachable alone = the dish; both fine but latency climbing = the path.
starlink.gotchas: The dish must be reachable: Starlink router in bypass mode or a route to 192.168.100.1. The API is unauthenticated LAN-only by design. Field names ride firmware releases - grpcurl's reflection heals drift that baked protobuf field numbers would not.

otlp.what: The OpenTelemetry inlet (superlog-otlp): an OTLP/HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:4318 accepting POST /v1/logs, /v1/metrics and /v1/traces in both application/json (OTLP/JSON) and application/x-protobuf (a hand-rolled bounded decoder). Anything OTel-instrumented joins the bench with one exporter stanza and no new SDK; each resource's service.name becomes the topic.
otlp.read: severityNumber -> level: 1-4 TRACE, 5-8 DEBUG, 9-12 INFO, 13-16 WARN, 17-20 ERROR, 21-24 CRITICAL; severityText is the fallback; absent is INFO. The OTel trace_id (hex) becomes the event's `trace` field, so it correlates with the bench's own withTrace() ids - /recent?trace= returns both worlds. Log attributes become string fields (droppedAttributesCount surfaced). Metrics: gauge and sum data points are DEBUG metric events {name, value}; histograms are summarized to count and sum with a '(summarized)' note - no invented percentiles. Spans are DEBUG events carrying the trace id, name, duration_ms and status - an inlet, not a span store.
otlp.gotchas: Port 4318 is the STANDARD OTLP/HTTP port, so a real local collector may already own it - move ours (--port / SUPER_LOG_OTLP_PORT) or theirs; EADDRINUSE says so and exits. Both http/json and http/protobuf are accepted (most SDKs default to protobuf). Success responses are the empty forms ({} for JSON, zero bytes for protobuf) so exporters never retry a delivery the bench already took; malformed input is 400, oversized is 413, neither crashes the server. Binds loopback - the hub has no auth.

playbooks.triage: Something is wrong on the bench. 1) hub_status - is the hub even up, did it drop frames. 2) list_streams - which topics are live and which carry errors. 3) tail_logs level=ERROR on the suspicious topic, narrow by contains. 4) If the event has a trace field, search_logs by that trace to see the whole story across streams. 5) Older than a few minutes? search_history. Never pull a full stream - filter first, always.
playbooks.follow-a-trace: One action, every tier: take the trace id from any event (request line, build start, file save) and query /recent?trace= via search_logs. Producers propagate traces across HTTP and builds join inbound traces, so one id returns the request, the queries it caused, the errors it raised and the file edits around it, in hub order.
playbooks.silent-stream: A stream that STOPPED is the failure most tools miss - a quiet server and a dead server look identical. list_streams shows what was recently live; compare against what should be. wait_for with a matching filter after you trigger an action; if it times out, the producer is down or never logged. superlog-alert silence rules cover this permanently.
playbooks.power-incident: The machine is hot/loud/slow: tail_logs topic=power. level=WARN shows threshold crossings (thermal speed limit, single-process hogs, watts over baseline). The DEBUG 'top by energy' events name the culprits with pid - correlate the pid against app streams. power.cpu_pct is aggregate (1258 = ~12.6 cores). speed_limit_pct < 100 means macOS itself is throttling.
playbooks.watch-a-download: A big fetch (Hugging Face model, dataset): dl.<host>.<label> carries dl.pct/dl.mb/dl.rate_mbs. One WARN = stalled --stall seconds, one ERROR = dead (3x that), INFO recovered = moving again. 'done:' is the success verdict. Percent dropping then racing after a producer restart is a re-stream, not loss.
